operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order's operative sentence in the held printing reads that the President exempts Joseph W. Austin from the provisions of section 204 and does "continue him in the service until March 1, 1938", and the recital states the same period ("continued in the service until March 1, 1938"). The President is the actor and the stated date is the end by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive of March 1, 1938 under owner ruling 2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; on the exclusive reading the exemption ends when March 1, 1938 begins. No earlier end is shown by any held source and no later order extends it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or
service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District
of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic
separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such
service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided,
That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this
section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that Joseph W. Austin, foreman
carpenter in the United States Capitol Building under the office of the Architect of
the Capitol, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of two years
by Executive Order No. 6976 of February 26, 1935, be further exempted from the
provisions of this section and continued in the service until March 1, 1938;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Joseph W. Austin from the provisions
thereof and continue him in the service until March 1, 1938.

Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF JOSEPH W. AusTIN From ComMPpuLsoRY RETIREMENT FOR
AGE

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S. C.,
sec. 715a), provides:

“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or
service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District
of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic
separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such
service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided,
That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this
section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that Joseph W. Austin, foreman
carpenter in the United States Capitol Building under the office of the Architect of
the Capitol, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of two years
by Executive Order No. 6976 of February 26, 1935, be further exempted from the
provisions of this section and continued in the service until March 1, 1938;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Joseph W. Austin from the provisions
thereof and continue him in the service until March 1, 1938.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

THe Wuite Houss,
February 27, 1937.

[No. 7565]

U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1997

research_rationale:
Executive Order 7565 of February 27, 1937 exempts Joseph W. Austin, foreman carpenter in the Capitol Building under the Architect of the Capitol, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404; 5 U.S.C. 715a) and continues him in the service for a fixed period ending March 1, 1938. The working text is the machine-read government printing in Executive_Orders_7262-8027 (scanned pages 272-273, closing number tag 7565), disclosed as a provisional working text under owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-transcription-as-text.md; original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. The order's own terms end the exemption on March 1, 1938. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md the end is recorded as the stated date, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends when March 1, 1938 begins, so its last day is February 28, 1938) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The four machine searches in the packet (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, and the held-text search on the person's name) each report no hit for this order; a name search of the held order texts that I ran separately found only this order and Executive Order 6976 of February 26, 1935, the earlier exemption this order's recital names.

No held source shows Austin's separation, death or retirement before March 1, 1938, so no earlier end is established and the stated date is the first end the held evidence supports. savings_residuals.reason: The order grants one named employee a time-limited exemption from automatic separation and contains no savings clause, delegation, reporting duty or other command that could survive March 1, 1938; the bounded searches found no later instrument and no statute or regulation that cites the order.
